messages:
inc-bot: INCIDENT ALERT — prod latency spike detected for tenant=zenova-prod in dedicated-pool-5. Pager: eng-oncall. root_ts=2002345678

maya (oncall-sre): Acked, I'm on it. Paging eng-runtime @leo. What's the visible customer impact?

leo (eng-runtime): Seeing 95p streaming latency jump 120ms -> ~1.8s, error rate +1.7%. Queue depth for zenova steadily growing. KV cache hit rate normal. Logs show long head-of-line batches.

maya (oncall-sre): Queue depth peaked ~420k tokens queued, scheduler reports high batch latency. Hypothesis: tenant max_batch_tokens set high (512) causing oversized batches and head-of-line blocking. Propose surgical change: set zenova max_batch_tokens -> 128 + enable per-tenant queue shaper. Also cap max_concurrent_requests to reduce bursts.

elllen (infra): (typo noted) which exact flags/command do you want me to run against config-store? I can patch live.

leo (eng-runtime): Use admin CLI: 
```
rcli tenant set-opts --tenant zenova-prod --opts '{"max_batch_tokens":128,"queue_shaper":true,"max_concurrent_requests":12}'
```
Then rolling restart scheduler workers on dedicated-pool-5: 
`kubectl rollout restart deploy/scheduler-worker -n pool-5 --selector=pool=dedicated-pool-5 --timeout=5m`

maya (oncall-sre): Running the CLI now.

deploy-bot: Patch applied to config-store: /tenants/zenova-prod -> {"max_batch_tokens":128,"queue_shaper":true,"max_concurrent_requests":12} (id: cfg-zz-2002). Rollout started.

maya (oncall-sre): Rolling restart in progress, 1/5 pods restarted... 3/5 pods restarted.

leo (eng-runtime): Logs (sampling):
```
[09:43:12] scheduler: tenant=zenova-prod batch_size=120 tokens=14500 latency=110ms
[09:44:03] scheduler: tenant=zenova-prod batch_size=64 tokens=7600 latency=90ms
```
Latency improving on the scheduler side.

maya (oncall-sre): Dashboard check: 95p down to ~210ms, error rate back to baseline. Throughput for zenova decreased ~15% (expected tradeoff).

kevin (solutions): Notifying Zenova support and SR owner now. Draft message: "We observed transient queuing causing elevated tail latency; we've applied a temporary config (max_batch_tokens=128 + queue shaping). This should reduce tail latency; we're following up with a performance tuning plan."

kevin (solutions): pinging customer channel.

maya (oncall-sre): Next steps: run a post-incident analysis to determine why zenova workload created large token accumulation — likely long sequences or bursty batched calls. Consider adaptive max_batch_tokens per pattern. Sam, you're next oncall in ~45m; handing off.

sam (oncall-sre): I have context. If it regresses, page me. I'll own the postmortem + follow-ups.

inc-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED — Pager cleared. Duration ~17m. Severity: P2. Customer impact summary: transient elevated tail latency for Zenova on dedicated-pool-5, no request loss, mitigated via per-tenant batching and queue shaping.

ellen (infra): I'll record the config diff in infra playbooks and schedule a rollback test for the change in staging.

leo (eng-runtime): Added a temporary canary policy: keep zenova max_batch_tokens=128 for 24h, auto-increase slowly if latency stable and throughput needed.

maya (oncall-sre): Thanks everyone. Handoff to Sam for writeup and customer communication trace.

sam (oncall-sre): Acknowledged. I'll post the incident notes to #incidents/zenova-2002345678 and draft the postmortem. :thumbsup:

kevin (solutions): :thumbsup:

ellen (infra): Leaving a note: capture metrics snapshot and attach to the incident thread.

maya (oncall-sre): Filed follow-up tasks: - run synthetic bursts in staging - instrument adaptive-batching experiment - schedule a tuning session with Zenova.

sam (oncall-sre): Closing live channel, will keep thread for postmortem drafts.
